title: Films, music, sport & free time
goal: Recommend a drama or a song, say what's better and what's the best ever, follow a cricket match with friends, and talk about your hobbies.
intro:
Half of all conversations between friends are about what you watched, heard or played: the drama everyone's hooked on, the new OST, last night's match. This unit gives you the words — most of them English loans with Urdu grammar wrapped around them — and the grammar to **compare** things properly.

You met سے and سب سے in unit 8. Here you go further: **کہیں بہتر** 'far better', **… جتنا اچھا نہیں** 'not as good as', **بہترین / بدترین** 'the best / worst', **اب تک کا سب سے** 'the … ever', and **جتنا … اتنا** 'the more…, the more…'.

grammar.title: Comparing in depth
grammar.body:
Unit 8 gave you the basic pattern: **X Y سے اچھا ہے** 'X is better than Y' (lit. X, from Y, is good). Now the variations people actually use:

**Better / worse:** **بہتر** 'better' (the Persian form, very common), or **زیادہ اچھا**: یہ اس **سے بہتر** ہے. 'Worse' is just **زیادہ برا** or **… سے بھی برا** 'even worse than'.

**Much / far / a bit:** **کہیں** 'far' — کہیں بہتر 'far better', کہیں زیادہ 'far more'; **بہت** 'much'; **تھوڑا** 'a bit': تھوڑا بہتر.

**Less … than:** **سے کم**: مجھے یہ اس **سے کم** پسند ہے 'I like this less than that'.

**Even more:** **اور بھی**: دوسرا سیزن **اور بھی** اچھا ہے 'the second season is even better'.

**As … as / not as … as:** **جتنا** after the thing you compare with, agreeing with the subject: نیا سیزن پرانے **جتنا** اچھا نہیں 'the new season isn't as good as the old one'; یہ فلم اس **جتنی** مشہور نہیں (فلم f). 'Like / the same as' is **جیسا / جیسی / جیسے**: باپ **جیسی** آواز 'a voice like his father's'.

**Note:** بہتر already means 'better', so careful speakers avoid زیادہ بہتر — though you'll hear it.

grammar.title: The best, the worst, the … ever
grammar.body:
**سب سے** + adjective = 'the most' (lit. 'than all'): سب سے اچھا 'the best', سب سے مشہور 'the most famous', سب سے زیادہ 'the most'.

**Persian superlatives** in **-ترین** are very common in speech: **بہترین** 'best, excellent', **بدترین** 'worst'. They don't change for gender.

**'Of / in'** is just **کا / کی / کے**, agreeing with the noun that follows: ٹیم **کا** بہترین کھلاڑی 'the best player in the team', اس سال **کی** سب سے بڑی فلم 'the biggest film of the year', دنیا **کا** سب سے… 'the … in the world'.

**'Ever'** = **اب تک کا / کی / کے** (lit. 'of until now'): **اب تک کی** سب سے اچھی فلم 'the best film ever'; **زندگی کا** بدترین میچ 'the worst match of my life'.

**Out of a group:** **… میں سے** 'out of': دونوں **میں سے** کون بہتر ہے؟ 'which of the two is better?'.

**Praise:** **ایک سے بڑھ کر ایک** 'each one better than the last' — said of songs, dishes, players.

grammar.title: The more…, the more…: جتنا … اتنا
grammar.body:
Urdu says 'the more…, the more…' with the pair **جتنا** jitnā '(as) much as' … **اتنا** utnā 'that much':

**جتنی** زیادہ پریکٹس کرو گے، **اتنا** اچھا کھیلو گے — 'The more you practise, the better you'll play.'

Both words agree like adjectives with the noun they go with: **جتنا / جتنی / جتنے**, **اتنا / اتنی / اتنے** (پریکٹس is feminine → جتنی; لوگ is plural → جتنے). When they just mean 'the more', with no noun, use the masculine **-ا** form.

Add **ہی** after اتنا for emphasis: جتنا دیکھتا ہوں، **اتنا ہی** پسند آتا ہے.

In quick speech the verbs often disappear: **جتنے لوگ، اتنا مزہ** 'the more people, the more fun'; فلم جتنی لمبی، اتنی بور.

**Fixed phrase:** **جتنی جلدی ہو سکے** 'as soon as possible'.

**Pronunciation:** in this pair, اتنا is usually said **utnā** (that much); as 'so / this much' on its own it's **itnā**. Same spelling.

culture:
**Cricket** is the one thing almost everyone in Pakistan talks about: street cricket with a taped tennis ball (ٹیپ بال), the league season when cities cheer for their teams, and Pakistan–India matches when the country stops. You'll be expected to have an opinion on the captain. Football is big in parts of Karachi (Lyari) and Balochistan, and many young people follow European clubs.

**TV dramas** (ڈرامے) are a shared national habit — families watch the 8 p.m. episode together, the title songs (OSTs) become hits, and people discuss the plot like real gossip. Saying **اینڈ مت بتانا!** is serious. Music runs from qawwali and ghazals to film songs, Pakistani pop and the music shows everyone shares online.

When recommending, friends use the infinitive: **ضرور دیکھنا!**, **یہ سننا!** Praise is generous (**بہترین**, **ایک سے بڑھ کر ایک**), and something mediocre is just **ٹائم پاس**. Most sport and entertainment vocabulary is English with Urdu verbs — میچ جیتنا, اسکور کرنا, سیزن دیکھنا — which makes it one of the easiest topics to join in.

lessons.title: What are you watching?

tip.title: Recommending: ضرور دیکھنا!
tip.body:
- The infinitive is a friendly 'do…' for later: **ضرور دیکھنا!** 'you must watch it!'
- 'Don't' = **مت** + infinitive: اینڈ **مت بتانا**.
- Episodes: **پہلی / آخری قسط**; نئی قسط کب **آئے گی**؟ (قسط is feminine).

lessons.title: Better or worse?

tip.title: Far better, not as good as
tip.body:
- **سے بہتر** better than · **سے کم** less than · **کہیں بہتر** far better · **تھوڑا بہتر** a bit better.
- Not as … as: **… جتنا اچھا نہیں** — جتنا agrees: فلم … **جتنی** مشہور نہیں.
- Out of two: **دونوں میں سے** کون بہتر ہے؟

lessons.title: Favourite songs

tip.title: The best: سب سے, -ترین
tip.body:
- **سب سے** + adjective = the most: سب سے **اچھا** گانا, سب سے **مشہور** گلوکار.
- Or **بہترین** best / **بدترین** worst (no gender change).
- 'Of / ever': **کا / کی / کے** agrees with the noun: اب تک **کا** بدترین گانا, اب تک **کی** سب سے اچھی فلم.

tip.title: Cricket talk
tip.body:
- Scores are runs **پر** wickets: ایک سو اسی **پر** پانچ = 180 for 5.
- **وکٹ گرنا** a wicket falls (وکٹ is feminine: وکٹ گر **گئی**).
- **چھکا مارنا** hit a six; win **by** = **سے**: پانچ وکٹوں **سے** جیتے.

sentences.roman: Pākistān kā iskor kyā hai?

lessons.title: Players and rivals

tip.title: The more…, the more…: جتنا … اتنا
tip.body:
- **جتنا** … **اتنا** (said utnā) = the more … the more.
- Both agree with their noun: **جتنے** لوگ, **اتنی** اچھی ٹیم; no noun → **جتنا / اتنا**.
- Add **ہی** for emphasis: اتنا **ہی** بہتر. Verbs are often dropped: جتنا بڑا مقابلہ، اتنا مزہ.

new: جتنا زیادہ سنو، اتنا اچھا لگتا ہے۔

sentences.native: جتنا اچھا کپتان، اتنی اچھی ٹیم۔
